title: Host pipeline: cooperative DMA pooling and thread-affinity to cut prefill/decode tail latency
creator: Amina Park
description:
Background: Host-side overhead during prefill->decode handoff is a dominant source of tail latency for short generation requests. Multiple teams have observed spikes caused by repeated pinned-buffer allocations, NUMA-unfriendly copies, and threadpool contention when many concurrent prefill requests race to schedule DMA + kernel launches. This ticket implements a cooperative host DMA pooling layer plus thread-affinity policies and a lightweight scheduler handoff that reduces copies, avoids unnecessary context switches, and reduces jitter in kernel selection latencies.

Goal: Deliver a host-side change that reduces median and p95 prefill-to-decode latency by >= 20% and p99 by >= 30% on our multi-GPU 8xA100 test cluster. Implementation should be safe to gate behind a runtime flag and include benchmarks and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Cooperative DMA pool implemented: reusable pinned host buffers with per-NUMA caches and bounded growth
Thread-affinity policy added to host threadpool: prefill threads pinned to NUMA local CPUs and decode threads pinned to GPU-affine CPUs
Scheduler handoff: zero-copy intent expressed via fd/eventfd and fast-path that avoids extra memcpy when KV cache present
Automated benchmark harness compares baseline vs new pipeline with synthetic and production-like workload; shows >=20% median and >=30% p99 improvement for short (<=128 tokens) requests
Feature gated and default-off with telemetry flags; rollout doc and rollback path in console
PRs merged and release notes written for runtime-1.20
steps: Design: finalize DMA pool API and per-NUMA caching strategy; define sizing heuristics (safety caps per worker)
Prototype: implement host-side pool and NUMA allocator in /host/infra, expose flag runtime.host_dma_pool=true
Threading: add affinity helpers and apply to prefill/decode worker pools; ensure Windows/other OS fallbacks
Scheduler: modify prefill->decode handoff to annotate buffer ownership and use eventfd fast-path for immediate kernel launch
Benchmarking: run microbench (short seq, many concurrent) and end-to-end regression against convai and embedder flows
Rollout: gated canary on dedicated cluster, monitor tail latency and token throughput, then widen
comments: 2025-02-10 Amina Park: Created ticket after triage with SRE and Runtime leads. Baseline dashboards attached. Key hypothesis: amortize dma allocation cost and reduce scheduler wakeups to cut tail latency.

2025-02-12 Diego Alvarez: Spike completed — prototype pool reduces allocation count by ~70% in synthetic prefill loop. Measured 12% median improvement locally. Posting spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Host+DMA+Pooling+Spike
2025-02-14 Performance team: Observed p99 still dominated by thread contention when concurrency > 200. Proposed NUMA-aware caches and pinning to avoid cross-socket copies.

2025-02-16 Diego Alvarez: Implemented per-NUMA free lists and added affinity pins for prefill workers. Initial runs: median -18%, p95 -22%, p99 -28% on 8xA100 synthetic test (workload: 512 concurrent short requests). Results uploaded to Grafana panel.
2025-02-18 Design review: PM and DX reviewed change; asked to add telemetry keys for pool hit/miss, allocation counts, and thread wakeup counts. Also requested safe fallbacks when pool exhausted.

2025-02-19 Diego Alvarez: Added telemetry and gating flag. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 — contains pool, affinity, and handoff fast-path. Seeking review from @sre-team and @runtime-owners.

2025-02-20 QA: Small canary planned for 2025-02-24 on dedicated-ci-5 cluster. If canary shows regressions, rollback via runtime flag and revert PR 2345. Added follow-up task to test Windows and macOS dev boxes for correctness.
